audit_findings.title: The 2028 Notes are treated simultaneously as debt and converted equity
audit_findings.magnitude: 9.955 million conversion shares, 11.3% of the 88.344585 million-share denominator; removing them alone would increase each per-share value by approximately 12.7% before interest, tax, settlement-election and capped-call effects
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation retains 2028 Notes interest in owner earnings while including conversion shares in fully diluted shares, producing a numerator and denominator belonging to different capital structures.
audit_findings.evidence: Dilutive potential common stock equivalents include the assumed exercise, vesting and issuance of employee stock awards using the treasury stock method, as well as common stock issuable upon assumed conversion of our convertible subordinated notes due 2023 (the “2023 Notes”) up until its maturity date on January 15, 2023, our convertible senior notes due 2025 (the “2025 Notes”) up until its maturity date on August 15, 2025, and our convertible senior notes due 2028 (the “2028 Notes”) using the if-converted method.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated internal inconsistency. An unconverted case should retain interest and exclude conversion shares; a converted case should add back the relevant after-tax interest and account for the issuer's settlement election and capped calls. The gross denominator effect is large enough to materially alter the per-share valuation.
audit_findings.action: Rerun separate converted and unconverted cases using the $261.0 million principal, 9.955 million conversion shares, applicable after-tax interest, cash/share settlement terms and capped-call payoff through the $33.985 cap.

audit_findings.title: The growth paths may miss a known 2027–2028 royalty-price reset
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; affected 2025 gross royalties were $250.302 million, comprising $204.021 million from RELVAR/BREO and $46.281 million from ANORO, equal to 60.9% of 2025 total revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower negotiated prices would reduce royalty revenue and owner earnings beginning in 2027 and 2028, affecting the explicit forecast and the earnings base entering terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: RELVAR ® /BREO ® ELLIPTA ® has been selected for negotiation under this program, with its negotiated MFP scheduled to take effect beginning January 1, 2027, and ANORO ® ELLIPTA ® has been selected in a subsequent negotiation cycle, with its negotiated MFP expected to take effect in 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The pricing resets are filed, dated events, while the valuation uses smooth 0%, 3% and 5% growth paths. Medicare exposure, negotiated prices, volume response and commercial spillover are not supplied, so the reduction cannot be measured, but the affected royalty stream is sufficiently large and the resets occur early enough to be reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the negotiated MFPs, Medicare sales mix, expected commercial spillover, volume elasticity and product royalty-tier calculations; model separate 2027 RELVAR/BREO and 2028 ANORO step-downs and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash acquired-R&D spending may disappear from operating-cash-flow owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.368 million, equal to 5.7% of the $163.9 million owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquired-IPR&D expense was added back as noncash in operating cash flow while the corresponding cash payment was classified as investing; an owner-earnings calculation based only on operating cash flow could therefore omit the outlay.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash provided by investing activities was partially offset by $60.9 million for purchases of trading securities, $17.5 million for purchases of equity and long-term investments, $9.4 million in cash paid for acquired in-process research and development assets, and $1.1 million for purchases of property and equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the cash outlay and its cash-flow classification, but the supplied record does not show whether the anchor calculation separately deducted it. It also does not establish whether this was a one-time acquisition or recurring replacement investment. The amount is meaningful relative to the anchor, but recurring valuation impact remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $163.9 million anchor line by line, verify whether the $9.368 million payment was deducted, and establish a filed history or operating forecast for recurring licensing, acquired-IPR&D and product-replacement spending before rerunning owner earnings.

audit_findings.title: The HCR royalty financing contains a contingent senior claim not represented by ordinary interest alone
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.582 million carrying obligation at 2026-06-30; 2025 cash royalties were $12.8 million versus $6.3 million of interest expense; the filed 2025 year-end acceleration amounts were $85 million or $185 million after subtracting $40 million of aggregate royalties paid
audit_findings.mechanism: Full cash royalties reduce owner earnings, while a triggered acceleration or foreclosure affects the equity bridge and the value of GIAPREZA-related assets; accounting interest alone may not capture either effect.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the terms of the La Jolla Royalty Agreement, if we are unable to meet certain obligations, including the obligation to use commercially reasonable and diligent efforts to commercialize GIAPREZA ® , HCR would have the right to terminate the La Jolla Royalty Agreement and demand payment of either $ 125.0 million or $ 225.0 million (depending on which obligation we have failed to meet) less aggregate royalties already paid to HCR.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual claim and its scale are demonstrated, but the record does not establish that owner earnings omitted principal-like royalty payments or that an acceleration trigger is probable. HCR has recourse only to GIAPREZA-related assets. The possible $185 million claim equals about 5.6% of base equity value, so the issue may be material, but present materiality cannot be established without the anchor reconciliation and trigger assessment.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to the entire HCR cash royalty payment, update cumulative royalties and the $125 million/$225 million acceleration balances through 2026-06-30, confirm the $61.582 million obligation within debt context, and stress GIAPREZA cash flows and foreclosure recovery under each trigger.

audit_findings.title: Strategic stakes may not be realizable at the bridge’s carrying values
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified downside on the $435.8 million bridge addition, which equals $4.93 per share and 13.1% of the $3.318 billion base equity value; the latest filing reports $315.960 million of Level 3 fair-value assets
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds strategic investments to equity at carrying value; liquidity discounts, taxes, stale measurement-alternative values, valuation-model uncertainty and correlated claims on the same investee can reduce realizable proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: There are uncertainties on the fair value measurement of the instruments classified under Level 3 due to the use of unobservable inputs and interrelationships between these unobservable inputs, which could result in higher or lower fair value measurements.
audit_findings.explanation: No specific misvaluation is demonstrated, but the bridge addition is large enough that a meaningful haircut could materially alter per-share value. The latest filing confirms substantial exposure to unobservable valuations, while several investments combine equity, warrants and debt claims on the same development-stage company. The actual downside remains unquantified because asset-level bridge composition, taxes and realizability are absent.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $435.8 million bridge asset by asset to 2026-06-30 filings; identify Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and measurement-alternative amounts; update quoted holdings to the valuation date; apply security-specific liquidity, tax and recovery adjustments; consolidate correlated claims by investee; and rerun the bridge under documented haircuts.
